paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this whole farewell is about: the LORD doesn't leave His people, even when they get it wrong. Israel asked for a king while the LORD their God was already their king (1 Samuel 12:12). They even admit, "we have added to all our sins the evil of asking for a king" (1 Samuel 12:19). And Samuel doesn't say "I told you so." He says, "Do not be afraid," and then, "the LORD will not abandon His people," because "He was pleased to make you His own" (1 Samuel 12:20, 22).

So the thing that keeps them going is not how good they've been. It's who the LORD is and what He's done. Samuel tells them to "consider what great things He has done for you" (1 Samuel 12:24). I think that's a good habit for us, baker. When you mess up, look back at what the LORD has already done, and let that pull you toward Him instead of away.

Samuel also shows what it looks like to stay faithful. He says it would be a sin against the LORD to stop praying for them, and he promises to keep teaching them "the good and right way" (1 Samuel 12:23). His record was clean, and he still kept loving and serving the people. Then comes the "Above all": "fear the LORD and serve Him faithfully with all your heart" (1 Samuel 12:24). Don't chase "worthless things that cannot profit you or deliver you," friend, because they're empty (1 Samuel 12:21). And the story isn't over, because Israel's new king is just getting started.
